claims.text: Equimolar or nearly equimolar CoCrFeNiTi can exist as a homogeneous single-phase FCC or near-FCC solid solution.
This starting state has favorable plasticity and machinability but relatively low hardness and strength.
The low hardness and strength are governed by intrinsically high dislocation mobility.
High dislocation mobility produces rapid stress-driven dynamic recovery.
Dynamic recovery prevents effective dislocation-density buildup despite significant plastic deformation.
Limited dislocation accumulation results in limited work hardening.
The alloy has a high-symmetry disordered lattice with low lattice friction.
Low lattice friction facilitates dislocation nucleation and motion.
The proposed lattice state facilitates dislocation cross-slip.
At room temperature, facile dislocation motion and cross-slip promote rapid dynamic recovery.
Lowering the test temperature will impede dislocation mobility and dynamic recovery.
Relative to room-temperature deformation, low-temperature deformation will produce a higher dislocation density.
Relative to room-temperature deformation, low-temperature deformation will produce greater strain hardening.
Relative to room-temperature deformation, low-temperature-tested samples will show higher measured hardness and strength.
The proposed mechanism is limited to monotonic elastic-plastic deformation of equimolar CoCrFeNiTi having a simple solid-solution microstructure.
If reduced-temperature samples fail to show higher dislocation density, greater work hardening, and increased hardness or strength, the proposed dynamic-recovery mechanism is falsified.

contradictions.description: The room-temperature group is identified as the baseline in the intervention and baseline fields, whereas the conditions field calls the reduced-temperature group the control.
